newsitem.title: CHINA: Timetable hard on info-tech liberalisation - Jiang.
newsitem.headline: Timetable hard on info-tech liberalisation - Jiang.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin said on Monday it would be very difficult to liberalise trade in information technology according to a fixed timetable, the official Xinhua news agency reported.
Xinhua quoted Jiang as making the remarks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Manila.
U.S. President Bill Clinton has been pushing Asia-Pacific leaders to strongly endorse his effort to conclude a global agreement on free trade in computers and telecommunications equipment by 2000.

Flexibility would be needed on the kind of products to be included in any liberalisation of information technology and efforts would be needed to eliminate barriers to technology transfer, Xinhua quoted Jiang as saying in an address.
The issue of information technology was very important for members of the forum, Jiang said.

"However, because of of the differences in the levels of economic development in the member economies, it is very difficult for the liberalisation in this field to be pushed forward in accordance with a timetable," Jiang said.
